<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|414|THE EPISTLE OF S. PAVL|CHA. XIII.}}</noinclude>& before the faith was preached among the Gentiles: by vvhich not onely euery other inferiour teachers doctrine was tried, but al the Apostles, and Euangelistes preaching, writing, interpreting (which is bere called prophecying) were of Gods Church approued and admitted, or disproued and reiected. This forme, by mouth and not by Scripture, euery Apostle deliuered to the countrie by them conuerted. For keeping of this forme, the Apostle before praised the Romanes, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''c. 6, 17''.}}and afterward earnestly warneth them by no mans plausible speache to be drawen from the same. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''c. 16, 17''.}}This he commendeth to Timothee, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Tim. 6, 20''.}}calling it his ''Depositum''. For not holding this fast and sure, he blameth the Galatians, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gal. 1, 6''.}}further also denouncing to him self or an Angel that should write, teach, or expound against that which they first receiued, Anathema, and commaunding alwaies to bevvare of them that taught otherwise. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Gal. 2, 1''.}}For feare of missing this line of truth, him self notwithstanding he had the Holy Ghost, yet lest he might haue preached in vaine and lost his labour, he went to conferre with Peter and the rest. {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Act. 15, 6.''}}for the fast keeping of this Rule of truth, the Apostles held Councels, and their successors by their example. For the holding of this Rule, and by the measure thereof, were al the holy Scriptures written. for and by the same, al the glorious doctors haue made their sermons, commentaries, and interpretations of Gods word: al writings and interpretations no otherwise admitted nor deemed to be of God, but as they be agreable to this Rule. {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Heretikes phantastical rule, or rather rules of faith, many and diuers one from an other.}}And this is the sure Analogie and measure of faith, set downe and commended to vs euery where for the Apostles tradition: and not the phantastical rule or square that euery Sectmaister pretendeth to gather out of the Scriptures falsely vnderstood and wrested to his purpose, by which they iudge of doctor, Scripture, Church, and al. Arius had by that meanes a rule of his owne, Luther had his false weightes, and Caluin his owne also. According to which seueral measure of euery Sect, they haue their expositions of Gods word: and in England (as in other infected Countries) they kept of late an apish imitation of this prophecying which S. Paul here and in other places speaketh of, and which was an exercise in the primitiue Church, measured not by euery mans peculiar spirit, but by the former Rule of faith first set downe by the Apostles. And therfore al this new phantastical Prophecying & al other preaching in Caluins schoole, is iustly by this note of the Apostle condemned, for that it is not according to, but quite against the Rule of faith.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''To yeld obedience and al other duties vnto Potestats: 8 to loue their neighbour vvhich is the fulfilling of the Lavv: 11 and specially to consider, that novv being the time of grace, vve must doe nothing that may not beseme day light.''}} {{dropinitial|L|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial L, a standing child.png|imgsize=155px|fl={{verse|chapter=13|verse=1}}}}ET {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Tit. 3, 1. 1. Pet. 2, 13.''}}* {{sup|‖}} euery soul be subiect to higher powers, for there is {{sup|‖}} no povver but of God. And those that are, of God are ordeined. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=2}}† Therfore he that resisteth the povver, resisteth the ordinance of God. And {{sup|‖}} they that resist, purchase to them selues damnation. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=3}}† for princes are no feare to the good worke, but to the euil. But wilt thou not feare the povver? Doe good: and thou shalt haue praise of the same. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=4}}† for he is gods minister vnto thee for good. But if thou doe euil, feare. for he {{sup|‖}} beareth not the svvord without cause. For he is Gods minister: a reuenger vnto vvrath, to him that doeth euil. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=5}}† Therfore be subiect of necessitie, not only for vvrath, but also for conscience sake. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=6}}† For therefore {{sup|‖}} you giue tributes also. for they are the ministers of God, seruing vnto this purpose. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=7}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 22, 21.''}}* Render therfore to al men their devv:

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Obedience to temporal rulers, & in what cases.}}∷ to vvhom tribute, tribute: to vvhom custom, custom: to whom feare, feare: to vvhom honour, honour.<noinclude>{{rh|||Ovve}}</noinclude>
